fenced_code.name: markup.fenced_code.block.carve
fenced_code.comment: The leading-whitespace capture is load-bearing twice over: the `end` pattern closes on the SAME indentation via \1, and a fence inside a list item is indented. Leading whitespace is ALLOWED, deliberately (carve-grammars#71). The strict column-0 rule makes an indented opener literal text at the top level, but the same opener indented INSIDE a list item is valid and common - verified against carve-rs: at the top level every one of these renders as a paragraph, and at a list item's content column every one opens its real block. A line-based grammar cannot tell those two apart; that needs block context, which only tree-sitter-carve has (its #38). So the choice is over-coloring the rare invalid case or under-coloring the common valid one, and every block rule here picks the same side - the asymmetry this used to have was an accident of anchoring, not a decision.

heading.name: markup.heading.carve
heading.comment: Leading whitespace is ALLOWED, deliberately (carve-grammars#71) - see the comment on `admonition` for the tradeoff this repeats. Restructured from a flat `match` into a `begin`/`end: "$"` construct (mirrors `table_row`, the existing precedent in this file for a single physical line that still needs recursive `patterns`) so a tag inside a heading's literal trailing brace run still scopes as a tag (carve-grammars#125): `# H {#id .cls}` has no real attribute block (headings take none), so the brace run is ordinary heading text, and `#id` inside it is still a tag construct - that half was already correctly NOT scoped as `attributes`, only the tag scope itself was missing. Uses `#heading_tag` (a `#tag` variant, see its own comment), not `#tag` directly, to stay out of the way of a heading cross-reference. Deliberately narrow: not the full `#inline` set table_row uses - headings are known (corpus 02-headings-4, 118) to support broader inline markup (emphasis, cross-references) that stays unscoped here, matching this repo's pattern of accepting a narrow, targeted fix over modeling everything at once (PR #129).

block_comment.comment: A %%% fence line is a delimiter plus an insignificant tail (spec PART 9 section 28): only the leading run of % is structural, so `%%% TODO` opens and `%%% end` closes. %%% carries no info string - a raw passthrough block is a CODE fence with an =FORMAT info string - so `%%% html` is a comment. The end backreference matches the opener width exactly, so %%%% nests %%%.
block_comment.name: comment.block.carve

admonition.name: meta.admonition.carve
admonition.comment: Leading whitespace is ALLOWED, deliberately (carve-grammars#71). The strict column-0 rule makes an indented opener literal text at the top level, but the same opener indented INSIDE a list item is valid and common - verified against carve-rs: at the top level every one of these renders as a paragraph, and at a list item's content column every one opens its real block. A line-based grammar cannot tell those two apart; that needs block context, which only tree-sitter-carve has (its #38). So the choice is over-coloring the rare invalid case or under-coloring the common valid one, and every block rule here picks the same side - the asymmetry this used to have was an accident of anchoring, not a decision. Restructured from a flat `match` into `begin`/`end` (carve-grammars#125): a div/admonition's opener and closer are on their own lines, so a per-line `match` left the body wide open to the full top-level pattern set - which incorrectly let `#abbreviation` fire inside a div (PART 9: abbreviation definitions are recognized at document level only; the sibling list-item and blockquote cases already read correctly, but only because their own line mechanics happen to block it, not because either detects the container). The closer backreferences the opener's captured colon run (`\1`), so it closes on an EXACT length match, matching PART 9's colon-fence depth rule (a longer or shorter run does not close it, which is what lets equal-length fences nest and `::::` hold `:::`) - mirrors the `fenced_code` begin/end precedent in this same file. `patterns` is the top-level pattern list minus `#frontmatter` (document-start only) and minus `#abbreviation` (the one construct this fix targets); everything else - headings (corpus 170), nested admonitions/divs via the `#admonition` self-include, lists, blockquotes, tables - keeps working inside a div exactly as before.

list_continuation.comment: A lone `+` at the list-marker column is the list-continuation marker (not a bullet -- `+` is never a bullet in Carve); it attaches the following flush-left block to the item.

list_item.comment: A marker line may carry several markers (`- - A` opens two nested lists), so scope each one, not only the line-anchored first. A BULLET MAY ALSO BE GLUED TO AN ATTRIBUTE BLOCK, and then the required space comes after the block, not after the marker - so `-{#x} item` and `*{.c} item` went uncoloured on a line that IS a list item, while the ordered rule beside it already had the branch (#126). The guard is that rule's, unchanged: content is still required past the block (`-{#x}` alone is a paragraph), and the block is spelled out rather than skipped with `\{[^}]*\}`, because a quoted value may hold a `}` and may escape its own quote. It is a LOOKAHEAD - consuming the block here would make this rule own those characters, so the attribute rule could no longer scope them. KNOWN LIMITATION, shared with every Carve TextMate grammar: `task_item` runs first and has no such branch, so the checkbox in `-{.c} [x] done` is not scoped; the bullet is. THE PAYLOAD MUST BE VALID, not merely brace-delimited: an invalid one means the `{` is literal content and the line is prose. `-{+a+} text` (corpus 90-list-item-attributes-6) and `1.{2=v} text` are paragraphs, while `-{} item` and `-{not attrs} item` are list items. A guard that accepted any brace run coloured the first two as lists. Identifiers are STRICT (PART 9 S14) and admit no colon, which is what carve-js does - Prism and highlight.js still admit one in their own attribute rules, a separate pre-existing divergence.

numbered_item.comment: Every ordered marker the language accepts, not only `1.`: decimal, single-letter and roman, with `.` or `)`, plus the BARE DOT (carve#472) - `.` alone continues the ordered sequence, and is the only marker allowed to drop its value. The bare form is also recognised glued to an attribute block (`.{#x}`), which is how corpus 174-bare-dot-ordered-markers-3 writes it. MARKER REQUIRES CONTENT, AND SO DOES THE ATTRIBUTE FORM: `1.{#x}` with nothing after the block is a paragraph, so the glued-block branch spells the block out in full rather than skipping it - a quoted run may contain `}` (`{title="a}b"} x` is a valid item) and may escape its own quote, so a `\{[^}]*\}` run stops in the wrong place. Anything less was tried and each attempt traded one broken shape for another (#85). A ROMAN RUN IS CASE-CONSISTENT: two classes, not one `[ivxlcdmIVXLCDM]`, which matched any mixture and coloured `Vim. text` and `Mix. text` as lists where carve-js renders paragraphs (#118). `mix.`, `civil.` and `did.` DO open lists, so the fix is the case split rather than rejecting multi-letter words. THE PAYLOAD MUST BE VALID, not merely brace-delimited: an invalid one means the `{` is literal content and the line is prose. `-{+a+} text` (corpus 90-list-item-attributes-6) and `1.{2=v} text` are paragraphs, while `-{} item` and `-{not attrs} item` are list items. A guard that accepted any brace run coloured the first two as lists. Identifiers are STRICT (PART 9 S14) and admit no colon, which is what carve-js does - Prism and highlight.js still admit one in their own attribute rules, a separate pre-existing divergence.

code_inline_multi.comment: Two or more backticks: inline code that may itself contain single backticks; closed by the same run length (\1).
code_inline_multi.name: markup.raw.inline.carve

critic_sub.name: markup.changed.carve
critic_sub.comment: Editorial substitution requires the `~>` arrow; a `{~x~}` with no arrow is forced strikethrough (PART 9 S22).

forced_strong.comment: Forced intraword bold (PART 9 S22). Content may contain the delimiter; the span ends at the closing `\*}`.

forced_italic.comment: Forced intraword italic (PART 9 S22). Content may contain the delimiter; the span ends at the closing `/}`.

forced_underline.comment: Forced intraword underline (PART 9 S22). Content may contain the delimiter; the span ends at the closing `_}`.

forced_strike.comment: Forced intraword strikethrough (PART 9 S22). Content may contain the delimiter; the span ends at the closing `~}`.

attributes_empty.comment: An empty attribute block is only valid glued to a preceding `]` (`[x]{}` -> x); a bare `{}` in prose is literal text (corpus 123).

attributes.name: meta.attributes.carve
attributes.comment: Strict identifier (spec PART 9 S14): a class/id/key may not start with a digit, so `{2=v}` stays literal text instead of scoping as an attribute block. An unquoted value may contain dots and colons.

heading_tag.comment: Used only inside `heading` (carve-grammars#125), not the shared `#tag` include: a heading's own inline set does not carry `#cross_ref`, so without this guard a heading cross-reference's `#id` (`</#id>`, grammar.ebnf `auto_text_link`) would be wrongly claimed as a tag - corpus 118 pins `# A </#a>` staying unscoped as a whole. `#cross_ref` is not added here instead because that would mean modeling the full cross-reference construct (and its `>` closer) inside headings, well past this ticket's scope; excluding the one shape that collides is the narrower fix.

literal_inline_multi.comment: A `!` prefix on two or more backticks: an inline literal that may itself contain single backticks; closed by the same run length (\2).

definition_list.comment: A `:` description line scopes only INSIDE an entry a real `:: ` term opened (carve-grammars#91) - a bare `:` line at the top level (no preceding term, or a term the separator rule disqualified, e.g. `::\tterm`) is prose and carries no scope. `begin` opens on a real term line (separator is a literal space per the tab-and-separator ruling on markup-carve/carve#698 - a tab never satisfies it); `end` closes on the next OTHER block opener (heading, list, quote, fence, hr, caption, table row), tolerating blank lines and lazy-continuation prose in between so a folded term (`term_continuation_line`) or a definition separated from its term by one blank line (corpus 25-definition-lists-7) still scope.

citation.comment: Citation group [@key]; ported from intellij-carve. Citation group: a bracket whose content contains at least one @key and has no (url)/[ref]/{attrs} tail. A leading + signals an integral/in-text citation. Items are ;-separated; each may carry a -/+ prefix and an optional , locator. The @key and the -/+ per-item markers are scoped distinctly, analogous to @mention but inside the citation bracket.

patterns.name: markup.citation.carve
patterns.comment: Match the whole citation bracket [+?...@key...] that is NOT followed by (, [, or { (which would make it a link, ref-link, or span). A lookahead for @ inside the brackets discriminates from plain spans and footnote refs.
Optional -/+ per-item modifier immediately before the @key
patterns.name: keyword.operator.citation.modifier.carve

callout_annotation.comment: Leading callout annotation line: <N> at the very start (with optional leading whitespace), followed by a space and annotation prose.
callout_annotation.name: markup.callout.annotation.carve

callout_marker.comment: Trailing callout marker inside a code line: <N> at the end of the line (optionally preceded by whitespace).
callout_marker.name: markup.callout.marker.carve
